newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends weak after failing to hold rallies.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends weak after failing to hold rallies.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled mostly lower after twice failing to maintain rallies, traders said.
Traders said decent-sized commercial buying was undermined by sizable commission house selling.
"The market failed twice in its attempt to rally on the slow pace of harvest. Inevitably, lower prices in Kansas City dragged Chicago wheat down, too," a KCBT trader said.
Reports of good quality characteristics in some initial samples of the Texas wheat crop were a possible source of pressure, traders said.
KCBT wheat had opened mostly steady and had traded both sides in choppy, early dealings amid uncertainty over the quality of the Texas harvest, traders said.
KCBT wheat settled 3-1/2 cents per bushel lower to 2-1/2 cents higher, with July down 3-1/2 cents at $3.84.
Traders said Continental Grain was a featured player, buying 1.5 million July bushels and also selling one million July. Refco sold 1.5 million July, traders said.
